spec.description: Search the catalogue and return a page of matching works, best match first.

request.title: SearchBooksRequest
request.description: The query, and which page of it to return.

q.description: The query. Free text, or a fielded Solr query such as `author:tolkien subject:fantasy`.

author.description: Restrict the search to author names.

page.description: Which page of results to return, counting from 1.

fields.description: Which fields to return on each result. Omit it and the API picks a default set; name them and each result carries only those, which is how a search response is kept small.

items.description: One field name, such as `key`, `title` or `author_name`.

sort.description: Sort order, such as `new`, `old`, `rating` or `editions`. Omit it for relevance.

language.description: Restrict results to one language, as a three-letter MARC code such as `eng`.

response.title: SearchResults
response.description: One page of results, and the counts around it.

numFound.description: How many works matched. Exact when `numFoundExact` is true, a lower bound otherwise.

numFoundExact.description: Whether `numFound` is an exact count rather than an estimate.

start.description: Index of the first result on this page, counting from 0.

num_found.description: The same number as `numFound`, under the name an older version of this API used.

q.description: The query as the search parsed it.

offset.description: The `offset` the request carried, or null when it paged by `page` instead.

documentation_url.description: Link to the search API's own documentation, returned on every response.

docs.description: The matching works, best match first.

items.title: SearchDoc
items.description: One matching work. Every field is optional: `fields` on the request decides which are present, and a work that has no cover or no fulltext simply omits those.

key.description: The work's Open Library key, such as `/works/OL893414W`.

author_key.description: Author keys, without the `/authors/` prefix, in the same order as `author_name`.

author_name.description: Author names, in the same order as `author_key`.

first_publish_year.description: Year the earliest known edition was published.

edition_count.description: How many editions of this work Open Library holds.

cover_edition_key.description: Key of the edition the cover was taken from.

has_fulltext.description: Whether the Internet Archive holds a scan whose text is searchable.

public_scan_b.description: Whether a scan is readable by anyone, rather than lendable.

ebook_access.description: How readable the work is: values seen include `no_ebook`, `printdisabled`, `borrowable` and `public`. Left a plain string rather than an `enum`, because Open Library publishes the vocabulary in prose and adds to it.

ia.description: Internet Archive identifiers of scans of this work.

language.description: Languages the work has editions in, as three-letter MARC codes.

items.description: One MARC language code, such as `eng`.

notes: The walk ends on a short page, not on `numFound`. A `total` terminator would be the richer declaration and the wrong one: `numFoundExact` exists because the count is sometimes an estimate, and the generated walk raises when a declared total moves between pages. A page holding fewer rows than `limit` is the last page under every one of the API's own modes, so that is what is declared.

The frame is kept rather than unwrapped: `numFound` and `numFoundExact` are things the caller asked for, so this is authoring rule 6's "keep the envelope" branch and there is no `envelope` block. The pagination paths are therefore relative to the frame, which is why `done.rows` is `docs`.

`page` and `offset` are two ways to say the same thing and the API accepts either. Only `page` is declared as the walk's index; `offset` is left out of the request entirely so a caller cannot send both and get a page neither of them asked for.
